title: Impact of Indoor Smoking Ban on Respiratory Health

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (municipality and period).  

Why:  
• We observe repeated outcomes (hospital admissions) for treated and control municipalities before and after the smoking-ban policy.  
• The policy is implemented only in the treated group and is time-invariant thereafter, fitting the canonical DID set-up.  

Key assumption (Parallel Trends):  
In the absence of the smoking ban, the trend in respiratory hospital admissions for treated municipalities would have been the same as for control municipalities. We will probe this with an event-study specification and a placebo-test robustness check.

---

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Impact of Indoor Smoking Ban on Respiratory Hospitalisations
############################################################
# Load packages
required_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest", "did")
for(p in required_pkgs){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s36_data.csv"
dt <- fread(data_path)

# 2. Canonical TWFE DID ----------------------------------------------------
# y ~ treated*post with municipality and period fixed effects
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treated*post | unit_id + period, 
                  data = dt, cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n===> Main DID result (TWFE) <===\n")
print(coeftable(did_twfe)["treated:postTRUE", ])   # coefficient & s.e.

# 3. Event-study / dynamic DID --------------------------------------------
# Convert period to factor to obtain leads/lags
# Assume smallest post period for treated units is the implementation date
dt[, treat_start := min(period[post == 1 & treated == 1])]
dt[, rel_time := period - treat_start]        # distance to treatment
# Create event-time dummies, omitting rel_time == -1 as baseline
for(k in sort(unique(dt$rel_time))){
  if(k != -1){
    dt[, paste0("e", k) := as.numeric(rel_time == k & treated == 1)]
  }
}
event_vars <- paste0("e", sort(unique(dt$rel_time))[sort(unique(dt$rel_time)) != -1])
form_event <- as.formula(
  paste("y ~", paste(event_vars, collapse = " + "), "| unit_id + period")
)
event_mod <- feols(form_event, data = dt, cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n===> Pre-trend (lead) coefficients <===\n")
print(coeftable(event_mod)[grep("^e\\-", rownames(coeftable(event_mod))), ])

# 4. Placebo test ----------------------------------------------------------
# Re-label period t = -2 as if it were the treatment date
dt[, placebo := (treated == 1 & period == (treat_start - 2))]
placebo_mod <- feols(y ~ placebo | unit_id + period, data = dt, 
                     cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n===> Placebo (fake treatment 2 periods before) <===\n")
print(coeftable(placebo_mod)["placebo", ])

# 5. Sensitivity: unclustered s.e. & no FE ---------------------------------
did_simple <- lm(y ~ treated*post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = dt)
cat("\n===> DID (unclustered s.e.) <===\n")
print(summary(did_simple)$coefficients["treated:post", ])

############################################################
# End of analysis
############################################################
```

---

## 3. Expected Findings  
• Sign: Negative. The smoking ban should reduce second-hand smoke exposure, lowering the number (and therefore the log) of respiratory hospital admissions.  

• Magnitude: A log-point reduction of roughly −0.05 to −0.10 (≈ 5–10 % decline) is typical in the public-health literature for similar clean-air ordinances.  

Interpretation: A coefficient of −0.08 would imply that the ban lowered respiratory admissions by about 8 % relative to the counterfactual trend in control municipalities.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in respiratory illness admissions over time between municipalities with and without the ban.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The indoor smoking ban is associated with an increase in hospital admissions for respiratory illnesses.
